title: Cytosolic Ca2+ measurements by ratiometric fluorescence microscopy in melanoma cells
protocol: Subculture melanoma cells as described in routine procedures.
Plate the subcultured cells into glass dishes for Fura-2 AM labeling and Ca2+ measurement by fluorescence microscopy.
Return the dishes with plated cells to the cell incubator at 37°C under an atmosphere of 5% CO2.
Allow the cells to adhere for 24 hours before proceeding to the next step.
Check cell morphology by optical microscopy.
Ensure cells are 70%–80% confluent.
Look for microbiological contaminants under optical microscopy.
Wash cells twice with 1.0 mL HBBS.
Add 1.0 mL HBBS to the washed cells.
Pipette 2.0 μL of Fura 2-AM stock solution to reach a final concentration of 2.0 μM.
Incubate in the dark for 30 min at 25°C.
Wash cells twice with 1.0 mL HBSS.
Add 1.0 mL HBBS to the washed cells.
Protect glass dishes from light using aluminum foil during transport.
Keep microtubes containing dyes and glass bottom dishes with labeled cells protected under aluminum foil.
Stain one dish at a time while keeping others in the CO2 incubator for gradual staining as needed.
Set up the Leica Application Suite (LAS v3.0) software for image acquisition.
Maintain the temperature in an acrylic environmental chamber at 37°C during the experiment.
Use an HCX PL Fluotar L 20×/0.40 dry objective for imaging.
Acquire images using a Hg lamp HXP R120W/45C VIS as light source.
Control all functions through LAS software commands.
Turn on the microscopy system.
Set the temperature to 37°C on the heat unit.
Select one channel for excitation at 340 nm with red as pseudo color.
Select another channel for excitation at 387 nm with green as pseudo color.
Select the emission filter cube for Fura 2 with a dichroic mirror at 409 nm and an emission band pass of 502–538 nm.
Select the “Calcium Imaging” calculator in LAS software’s “Quantify” tab.
Input a ratio formula for channel 1 (340 nm)/channel 2 (387 nm).
Correct the fluorescence background in the window.
Convert relative ratio 340/387 nm into absolute Ca²⁺ concentrations using the Grynkiewicz equation.
Position the glass bottom dish containing labeled cells under the microscope.
Find and focus on the sample in the bright field.
Adjust the fluorescence emission by controlling exposure and gain.
Use saturation indicator to ensure optimal settings.
Set the time course and read interval for the experiment.
Use a reading of 20 minutes every 5 seconds for melanoma cells under thapsigargin challenge.
Establish the time course based on the stimuli used, such as drugs, inhibitors, activators, protein silencing, or comparison among different cell lines.
Pipette the drugs or challenges directly into the dishes during measurements.
Record changes in real-time during the experiment.
Adjust the fluorescence excitation of red pseudo color (channel 1, 340 nm) to the lowest possible value.
Adjust the fluorescence excitation of green pseudo color (channel 2, 387 nm) to the highest possible value without saturation.
Dilute stock solutions of drugs or modulators in HBSS medium for addition during recording.
